Context
The assembled output of ContextEngine.assemble(java.lang.String, java.util.Map<java.lang.String, java.lang.Object>): every configured provider's result, namespaced by provider id so two providers can never silently clobber each other's keys, plus a flattened merged view for the common case where callers just want one map to feed into feature extraction.
ContextCache
Bounded, TTL-based cache for assembled Contexts, keyed by the request key (entity id, session id, etc.) — the "Context Cache" layer: avoid re-assembling context (parallel provider fan-out, each with its own network round trip) on every request when the underlying context hasn't changed since the last one.
ContextEngine
Assembles context from every configured ContextProvider in parallel before inference — the entry point for otter-stream-context.
ContextEngine.Builder
 
ContextProvider
A source of context to assemble before inference — the generalized parent abstraction behind otter-stream-context.
ContextResult
One provider's contribution to an assembled Context — its data (if it succeeded), how long it took, and its failure (if it didn't).
ConversationMemoryProvider
Conversation/session memory for RAG applications — the "session/user context" and "memory" piece a RAG pipeline needs: what has this session/user already said, so the model has conversational context rather than seeing each message in isolation.
ConversationTurn
One turn in a conversation — the unit ConversationMemoryProvider stores and retrieves.

DecisionEngineConnector
Extension point for delegating decisions to an external enterprise decision engine — Drools/Red Hat Decision Manager (KIE Server), Camunda DMN, IBM ODM, or any other system that accepts a fact/input and returns a decision — rather than evaluating rules in-process via RuleEngine.
DecisionKafkaSerializationSchema
Serializes rule-engine Decisions to JSON for a Flink KafkaSink — the natural pairing with InferenceResultKafkaSerializationSchema: publish the raw inference result to one topic and the post-rule-engine decision to another (or the same topic, differently keyed), so downstream consumers (case management, alerting, audit log) don't need to embed rule logic themselves.
DefaultModelRegistry
Simple in-memory ModelRegistry implementation: configurations are registered programmatically (typically at application startup) and resolved by exact version or, when unversioned, by the lexicographically-highest registered version string.
DefaultRuleEngine
The concrete RuleEngine used regardless of where the RuleSet came from (YAML, properties, or a hand-written RuleSetSource) — all three configuration paths converge here.
DeploymentException

DroolsDecisionEngine
Stateless Drools-based decision engine.
DroolsDecisionEngineConnector
DecisionEngineConnector backed by an embedded Drools KIE session — for teams running Drools in-process rather than fronting it with a KIE Server REST endpoint (use RestDecisionEngineConnector in otter-stream-rules for that case instead, with no Drools dependency at all).
DroolsDecisionEngineConnector.InferenceFact
Fact inserted into the KIE session — the input side of the rules.
DroolsDecisionEngineConnector.RuleDecision
Fact your DRL rules insert as their conclusion — the output side.
DynamicLoader
Polls a ModelRegistry on a per-model schedule and automatically deploys newly discovered versions through a LifecycleManager — this is the "dynamic loading" milestone: instead of an operator calling deploy() by hand every time a new model version is published, DynamicLoader notices it and rolls it out on its own, going through the same validate → warm → atomic swap → retire path as a manual deployment.

ExecutionTarget

ExecutionTargetAware
Implemented by an InferenceEngine that supports running on more than one ExecutionTarget and wants ExecutionTargetManager to automatically move it between them based on utilization.
ExecutionTargetManager
Watches ExecutionTargetAware engines on a fixed tick and automatically switches an idle GPU-resident engine back to CPU, freeing GPU memory/compute for other work — the "scale down or switch off the feature when operations return to normal" behavior.
Experiment
A named A/B test between a model's current primary ("control") and a candidate version ("variant"), running via OtterRuntime's existing canary mechanism (LifecycleManager.deployCanary, Milestone 6) — this class adds naming, lifecycle tracking, and (via ExperimentManager) outcome recording and statistical comparison on top of that existing traffic-split machinery.
ExperimentException

ExperimentManager

ExperimentOutcome

ExperimentStatus
